reference.title: Prostate carcinoma types (WHO 5th edition)
reference.intro: WHO 5th edition (2022) recommends diagnosing ductal adenocarcinoma on radical prostatectomy only when >= 50% of the tumour has ductal morphology; otherwise report acinar adenocarcinoma with ductal features.

groups.heading: Acinar adenocarcinoma, conventional (usual)
points: Discrete, fused, cribriform or solid infiltrating malignant acini lacking a basal cell layer.
Graded using Gleason patterns 3–5 and WHO/ISUP Grade Groups 1–5.

images.caption: Acinar adenocarcinoma: discrete infiltrating glands lacking a basal cell layer (Gleason score 3+3=6)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2a

groups.heading: Ductal adenocarcinoma
points: Large papillary and cribriform glands lined by tall pseudostratified columnar cells with elongated hyperchromatic nuclei.
On radical prostatectomy, requires >= 50% ductal morphology; graded as Gleason pattern 4 (or pattern 5 if comedonecrosis is present).

images.caption: Ductal adenocarcinoma of the prostate: tall pseudostratified columnar epithelium with elongated hyperchromatic nuclei forming papillary and cribriform architecture (graded as Gleason pattern 4) (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron

groups.heading: Intraductal carcinoma of the prostate (IDC-P)
points: Malignant proliferation filling and expanding pre-existing ducts with retained basal cells (p63 / 34betaE12).
Pure IDC-P without invasive carcinoma is not assigned a Gleason grade.

images.caption: Expanded duct filled by a dense cribriform proliferation of atypical cells (H&E, x100)
images.credit: Destouni et al., Cancers 2022, Fig 3a (cropped)

groups.heading: Treatment-related neuroendocrine / small cell & rare subtypes
points: Small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (synaptophysin/INSM1+, TTF-1 often+, PSA/NKX3.1 usually lost), sarcomatoid carcinoma and pleomorphic giant cell adenocarcinoma are aggressive variants.
Do not assign a Gleason score to pure neuroendocrine, squamous or basal cell carcinoma.

reference.title: Gleason patterns 3, 4 and 5 (radical prostatectomy)
reference.intro: On radical prostatectomy, the Gleason score is primary + secondary pattern. Unlike needle biopsy, a minor higher-grade pattern comprising < 5% of the tumour is recorded as a minor (tertiary) pattern rather than replacing the secondary grade.
reference.noteTop: 5% rule (radical prostatectomy only): >= 5% higher-grade pattern enters the Gleason score; < 5% is reported as a minor (tertiary) pattern (e.g. 3+4=7 with minor pattern 5).

groups.heading: Pattern 3 — discrete, separate glands
points: Well-formed individual glands surrounded by stroma, each with a single cell layer and separate lumen.

images.caption: Gleason score 3+3=6: discrete, separate, variably sized glands, each with its own lumen
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2a

links.label: ExpertPath: Prostate Cancer Grading (Gleason / Grade Group)

groups.heading: Pattern 4 — poorly formed, fused, cribriform or glomeruloid
points: Poorly formed glands (absent/abortive lumina at 10x), fused glands sharing walls, cribriform sheets with punched-out lumina, or glomeruloid tufts.
Report percentage of pattern 4 for all Gleason score 7 tumours (CAP 4.3.0.0).

images.caption: Poorly formed glands with incomplete or absent lumina (Gleason score 4+4=8)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2f

images.caption: Fused glands sharing a common wall; cytoplasmic vacuoles present (Gleason score 4+4=8)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2d

images.caption: Glomeruloid glands: intraluminal cribriform tufts attached at one edge (Gleason score 4+4=8)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2e

images.caption: Irregular cribriform glands (Gleason score 4+4=8)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2c

links.label: ExpertPath: Prostate Cancer Grading (Gleason / Grade Group)

groups.heading: Pattern 5 — sheets, cords, single cells, comedonecrosis
points: Solid sheets, cords, single infiltrating cells, or unequivocal comedonecrosis within solid/cribriform nests.

images.caption: Solid sheets of tumour cells without gland formation (Gleason score 5+5=10)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 3a

images.caption: Cords of tumour cells (Gleason score 5+5=10)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 3b

images.caption: Individually infiltrating tumour cells (Gleason score 5+5=10)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 3c

images.caption: Cribriform glands, some with central comedonecrosis (Gleason score 4+5=9)
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 3d

groups.heading: Borderline 3 vs 4 — favour the lower grade
points: Avoid overcalling tangentially sectioned pattern 3 glands as pattern 4; look at adjacent levels and neighbouring well-formed glands.

images.caption: Bordering 3+3=6 with tangential cuts against 3+4=7 with poorly formed glands; the ISUP panel favoured 3+3=6 (H&E, x20 objective)
images.credit: Egevad et al., Virchows Arch 2020, Fig 3a (cropped)

fields.help: Radical prostatectomy 5% rule: record a higher-grade pattern < 5% here rather than upgrading the Gleason score.

fields.label: Intraductal carcinoma (IDC-P)
options: Present, IDC not incorporated in grade

reference.title: Intraductal carcinoma of the prostate (IDC-P)
reference.intro: IDC-P expands pre-existing ducts with retained basal cells. GUPS recommends excluding IDC-P from the Gleason grade; ISUP recommends incorporating it when associated with invasive cancer — CAP 4.3.0.0 asks you to state which convention was used.

groups.heading: IDC-P criteria and basal cell confirmation
points: Expansile solid, dense cribriform or comedo proliferation inside pre-existing ducts with retained p63 / 34betaE12 basal cells.

images.caption: Expanded duct filled by a dense cribriform proliferation of atypical cells (H&E, x100)
images.credit: Destouni et al., Cancers 2022, Fig 3a (cropped)

images.caption: AMACR (brown) with p63 (pink) double stain: strong cytoplasmic AMACR with a preserved p63-positive basal layer
images.credit: Compérat et al., Cancers 2024, Fig 1B (cropped)

groups.heading: IDC-P vs invasive cribriform carcinoma
points: Basal cell IHC (p63 / HMWCK) separates IDC-P (basal cells retained) from invasive cribriform carcinoma (basal cells absent) when grade would change.

images.caption: IDC-P glands with cribriform morphology surrounded by invasive carcinoma glands
images.credit: Surintrspanont & Zhou, Cancers 2023, Fig 2A (cropped)

images.caption: p63 (brown): the intraductal glands retain basal cells while the invasive glands lack them
images.credit: Surintrspanont & Zhou, Cancers 2023, Fig 2B (cropped)

reference.note: ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

reference.title: Cribriform pattern 4 (ISUP / WHO 5th)
reference.intro: Invasive cribriform pattern 4 independently predicts biochemical recurrence and metastasis in Gleason score 7–8 prostate cancer.

groups.heading: ISUP definition of cribriform pattern 4
points: Confluent sheet of contiguous tumour cells punched by multiple lumina, visible at 10x, with no intervening stroma or mucin.

images.caption: Confluent sheets of tumour cells forming cohesive trabeculae with punched-out lumina and no intervening stroma (H&E, 100x)
images.credit: Compérat et al., Cancers 2024, Fig 2

links.label: ExpertPath: Prostate Cancer Grading (Gleason / Grade Group)

groups.heading: Large / complex cribriform architecture
points: Large cribriform glands carry the strongest adverse prognostic significance; report cribriform growth as Present in Gleason 7 and 8 tumours.

images.caption: Large, complex cribriform structure invading periprostatic adipose tissue (x100)
images.credit: Destouni et al., Cancers 2022, Fig 4b (cropped)

groups.heading: Mimics — not cribriform
points: Glomeruloid tufts (attached at one point; still pattern 4), basal cell hyperplasia, and clear cell cribriform hyperplasia are not invasive cribriform carcinoma.

images.caption: Glomeruloid glands: the intraluminal tuft stays attached at one edge, so this is not cribriform
images.credit: Gordetsky & Epstein, Diagn Pathol 2016, via Wikimedia Commons, Fig 2e

images.caption: Basal cell hyperplasia with a cribriform pattern (x100)
images.credit: Destouni et al., Cancers 2022, Fig 1b (cropped)

fields.label: Extraprostatic extension (EPE)
fields.help: Any EPE (focal or nonfocal) assigns pT3a.

reference.title: Extraprostatic extension (pT3a) and seminal vesicle invasion (pT3b)
reference.intro: EPE is tumour extending beyond the confines of the prostate gland into periprostatic soft tissue (adipose tissue, perineural spaces of neurovascular bundles, or desmoplastic bulging beyond the prostatic contour).

groups.heading: Extraprostatic extension (pT3a): focal vs nonfocal
points: Focal EPE: only a few neoplastic glands outside the prostate in 1–2 slides (or <= 0.6 mm radial / <= 1 HPF).
Nonfocal (established) EPE: more extensive extraprostatic tumour beyond focal criteria.
Pitfall: at the apex and anteriorly the prostatic capsule is poorly defined and benign skeletal muscle intermixes with prostate — tumour in skeletal muscle alone at the apex is NOT EPE.

images.caption: Extraprostatic extension (pT3a): infiltrating Gleason pattern 4 prostatic adenocarcinoma extending into periprostatic adipose tissue (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron

images.caption: Large, complex cribriform structure invading periprostatic adipose tissue (x100)
images.credit: Destouni et al., Cancers 2022, Fig 4b (cropped)

groups.heading: Microscopic urinary bladder neck invasion (pT3a)
points: Tumour infiltrating thick smooth muscle bundles of the bladder neck without residual benign prostatic glands.
Under AJCC 8th edition, microscopic bladder neck invasion is pT3a (NOT pT4).

groups.heading: Seminal vesicle invasion (pT3b)
points: Requires invasive carcinoma infiltrating the muscular wall of the extraprostatic seminal vesicle.
Tumour confined to the perivesicular fat or ejaculatory duct without seminal vesicle muscular wall invasion is pT3a (EPE), NOT pT3b.

images.caption: Benign seminal vesicle epithelium: golden-brown lipofuscin pigment and degenerative nuclear pleomorphism; seminal vesicle invasion (pT3b) requires tumour invading the muscular wall of the seminal vesicle (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron

reference.title: Radical prostatectomy surgical margins (CAP 4.3.0.0)
reference.intro: A surgical margin is positive ONLY when invasive carcinoma cells directly touch the inked resection surface. Close proximity (< 0.1 mm) without ink contact is reported as uninvolved.

groups.heading: Limited (< 3 mm) vs non-limited (>= 3 mm) positive margin
points: Measure the linear extent of ink contact (mm) — cumulative length >= 3 mm independently increases biochemical recurrence risk.
Specify all anatomical locations and whether positive margins are unifocal or multifocal.

groups.heading: Gleason pattern at positive margin(s)
points: Record the highest Gleason pattern touching ink (Pattern 3 vs Pattern 4 or 5) — pattern 4/5 at the margin carries higher recurrence risk than pattern 3 alone.

groups.heading: Intraprostatic (capsular) incision vs margin positivity in EPE
points: A positive margin inside an area of organ-confined tumour (intraprostatic incision) does NOT upstage pT2 to pT3a.
Record whether margin positivity occurs within an area of extraprostatic extension (pT3a).

reference.note: Criteria follow CAP Prostate Radical Prostatectomy 4.3.0.0 and ISUP guidelines. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.
